sources.title: Pearson Chem CP7b: Testing for anions (2017)
sources.read: Entire one-page original practical sheet rendered and actually viewed.
sources.supports: Known versus unknown samples, acid-first sequence, carbonate interference and reagent choice. No quantitative constants taken.

limits: AnionEvidence is an endpoint net stoichiometric allocation. Partial H+ budgets do not claim an acid-base equilibrium composition: bicarbonate, pH, Ksp and kinetics are not solved.
Gas markers have persistent IDs and make one finite exit. Their count and route are illustrative, not CO2 molecular count or generation rate.
Known textbook comparisons do not identify arbitrary unknown mixtures. Full acid disappearance and target persistence use the textbook dilute conditions.
Metal ions released from carbonate remain in the aqueous budget; carbon and both metal accounts are independently conserved.
